# 2 Kings Chapter 7 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 228r–228v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_007_page_001.jpg, 2KI_007_page_002.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Elisha said, "Hear the word of the LORD. Thus says the LORD: 'Tomorrow about this time, a seah of fine flour shall be sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria.'"

**2** Then the officer on whose arm the king was leaning answered the man of God, "Even if the LORD should make windows in heaven, could this thing be?" Elisha said, "You shall see it with your own eyes, but you shall not eat of it."

**3** Now there were four men with leprosy at the entrance of the city gate, and they said to one another, "Why are we sitting here until we die?

**4** If we say, 'Let us enter the city,' the famine is in the city and we shall die there. And if we sit here, we die also. So come, let us go over to the camp of the Arameans. If they spare us, we shall live; if they kill us, we shall but die."

**5** So they arose at twilight to go to the camp of the Arameans. But when they came to the edge of the camp, there was no one there.

**6** For the Lord had caused the army of the Arameans to hear the sound of chariots and horses — the sound of a great army — so that they said to one another, "The king of Israel has hired the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to come against us."

**7** So they fled at twilight, abandoning their tents, their horses, and their donkeys — leaving the camp just as it was — and fled for their lives.

**8** When the lepers came to the edge of the camp, they entered a tent, ate and drank, and carried off silver, gold, and garments, and went and hid them. Then they came back and entered another tent, carried off more, and went and hid it.

**9** Then they said to one another, "We are not doing right. This is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent. If we wait until morning light, punishment will overtake us. Come, let us go and tell the king's household."

**10** So they went and called to the gatekeepers of the city and told them, "We went to the camp of the Arameans, and there was no one there — not a sound of anyone — only the horses tied and the donkeys tied and the tents just as they were."

**11** The gatekeepers called out, and it was told within the king's household.

**12** The king arose in the night and said to his servants, "Let me tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know that we are hungry, so they have left the camp to hide in the open country, thinking, 'When they come out of the city, we shall take them alive and get into the city.'"

**13** One of his servants answered, "Let some men take five of the remaining horses — they will fare no better than the rest of Israel who are perishing — and let us send and see."

**14** So they took two horse-drawn chariots, and the king sent them after the Aramean army, saying, "Go and see."

**15** They followed them as far as the Jordan, and the whole way was littered with garments and equipment that the Arameans had thrown away in their haste. The messengers returned and told the king.

**16** Then the people went out and plundered the camp of the Arameans. So a seah of fine flour was sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, according to the word of the LORD.

**17** Now the king had appointed the officer on whose arm he leaned to have charge of the gate, and the people trampled him in the gate, and he died — just as the man of God had said when the king came down to him.

**18** For when the man of God had said to the king, "Two seahs of barley shall be sold for a shekel, and a seah of fine flour for a shekel, about this time tomorrow in the gate of Samaria,"

**19** the officer had answered the man of God, "Even if the LORD should make windows in heaven, could such a thing be?" And he had said, "You shall see it with your own eyes, but you shall not eat of it."

**20** And so it happened to him, for the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Chapter 7 answers the theological crisis of 6:33 ("Why should I wait for the LORD?") with dramatic irony: deliverance comes not through military might or royal initiative, but through four lepers who have nothing left to lose. The structure is built on reversal — famine becomes feast, silence becomes proclamation, doubt becomes deadly. The officer's fate is the chapter's moral pivot: skepticism toward the divine word results not in mere disappointment but in death at the very threshold of fulfillment. The lepers' declaration "This is a day of good news" (*yom besorah*) is one of the Hebrew Bible's most resonant phrases — outcasts bearing the announcement of salvation.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — Measurement rendering: Hebrew units vs. modern equivalents
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "a seah of fine flour" (Hebrew unit retained)
- **PNEUMA:** "six quarts of fine flour" (converted to modern measure)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "a seah of fine flour" — retain the Hebrew unit. The *seah* is a recognized biblical measure; converting to modern equivalents introduces false precision and loses the ancient texture.

### V.2 — "windows in heaven" vs. "floodgates in the sky"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "windows in heaven"
- **PNEUMA:** "floodgates in the sky"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "windows in heaven" — *arubbot* means "windows/lattice openings," not floodgates. The literal image should be preserved; it connects to Genesis 7:11 and Malachi 3:10.

### V.4 — "we shall but die" vs. "we were going to die anyway"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "we shall but die"
- **PNEUMA:** "we were going to die anyway"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "we shall but die" — the formal phrasing preserves the solemn resignation of the Hebrew. PNEUMA's version, while vivid, is too casual for the gravity of the moment.

### V.13 — Treatment of the textually difficult verse
- **EMET:** Very literal with repetition preserved
- **LOGOS:** Smoothed slightly: "those that are left will fare like the whole multitude"
- **PNEUMA:** Heavily paraphrased: "they're going to die like the rest of us anyway"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** Follow LOGOS — smooth the repetition for readability while preserving the servant's essential argument.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
